title: inference-margin-compendium-anjali-rao-2027-11-07
content:
Quick brain-dump / reading compendium focused on designing small, repeatable microbench protocols that expose marginal costs (latency + hallucination) of inference strategies. Mostly notes-to-self; plan to turn this into a tiny repo + a reproducible notebook for the team.

Context and motivation:
- We optimize for cost and reliability at Redwood; most public papers report aggregate throughput/average latency. But product-facing regressions often appear in the tail and in semantic failure modes (hallucination, repetition) under specific eviction/batching regimes.
- Want a compact set of micro-experiments that: 1) isolate KV/prefix eviction effects, 2) measure marginal token cost and tail latency per-request in mixed loads, 3) correlate token-level perturbations with downstream hallucination severity.

Reading list + high-level takeaways (curated):
1) "Adaptive KV Sharding for Long-Context Inference" (arXiv 2026) — key idea: selective eviction by recency+importance score. Takeaway: even conservative importance scoring can reduce cumulative token compute by 15% w/o material change in perplexity; failure modes concentrated on early prefix-dependent facts.
2) "Routing Mixture-of-Experts in Latency-Sensitive Systems" (SysML workshop, 2027) — tradeoff: expert sparsity reduces compute but amplifies variance in tail latency due to straggling experts and network cross-talk. Takeaway: deterministic routing + bounded in-flight tokens reduces worst-case tails.
3) "Quantization Stability Under Incremental KV Updates" (blog + supporting repo) — quantized KV representations drift when new tokens are appended to cache; stability depends on quantization scheme and refresh cadence. Takeaway: periodic small re-quant steps keep drift low; aggressive 4-bit schemes need occasional recalibration.
4) "Hallucination Cost Metric for Production" (paper + appendix) — propose a graded severity rubric for hallucination (benign/incorrect/confident-dangerous). Takeaway: measuring frequency alone misses impact; weight by user-visible severity.
5) "Microbench Patterns for Per-Token Tail Latency" (internal tech note by DevInfra) — practical harness designs with synthetic traces. Takeaway: synthetic traces must match prefix-length distribution and burstiness to be meaningful.

Synthesis — recurring themes:
- Distribution mismatch kills signal: naive microbench that only uses uniform prefix lengths or IID prompts underestimates tail latency and hallucination frequency.
- Small implementation details (routing hysteresis, token prefetch, quantization flip thresholds) cause outsized UX regressions.
- There exists a narrow regime where cost wins (batching/quantize) but hallucination severity increases nonlinearly; need joint metrics.

Experiments to run (priority order):
1) Eviction-sweep microbench (priority: high)
   - Goal: quantify marginal tail latency and hallucination-impact when varying eviction policies: LRU, recency+importance, fixed-window, token-importance threshold.
   - Setup sketch: replay a corpus of 5k real customer sessions (anonymized) with preserved prefix lengths and timestamps. Interleave 20% cold-start queries to simulate churn.
   - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 token-latency, tokens-per-second cost, hallucination-rate (graded by severity rubric), change-in-generation perplexity by prefix position.
   - Quick pseudo steps: 
     * checkout proto-microbench branch "evict-sweep"
     * generate trace: python tools/trace_gen.py --source customer-sample-2027-10 --preserve-timestamps --out traces/evict.json
     * run harness: ./bench/run.sh --model rdx-3b-q4 --trace traces/evict.json --eviction LRU --out results/lru.json

2) MoE routing determinism stress (priority: med-high)
   - Vary routing: deterministic top-k vs soft routing with temperature; measure tail and request variance.
   - Add synthetic straggle events to simulate slow experts.
   - Metric of interest: %requests that exceed SLA and degradation in output token quality for those requests.

3) Quantization incremental stability (priority: med)
   - Frequent small appends to KV followed by reconvergence checks. Track token-level drift using a short probe prompt bank.
   - If drift > threshold, perform in-place re-quantization and measure cost of that maintenance operation.

Evaluation design notes (how to measure hallucination impact):
- Use the graded rubric from the paper: map model outputs into {info-mismatch, plausible-but-false, confidently-false}. Weight them [0.5, 1.0, 2.0] respectively to compute a severity-weighted hallucination score.
- For edge cases, add human-in-the-loop spot checks (10% of high-severity outputs) to estimate false negatives.
- Instrument downstream product signals (if available): click-rate on suggested content, user correction rate, support ticket flags (sparse but useful).

Quick hypotheses to validate (for each experiment above):
- H1: Importance-aware eviction reduces average compute by ~12–20% while increasing high-severity hallucination by <5% if importance scoring uses attention-over-history + recency decay.
- H2: Deterministic MoE routing with small routing caches reduces p99 by ~30% compared to stochastic routing under mixed loads.
- H3: Periodic 8-bit re-quantization amortized monthly keeps hallucination drift near baseline for 4-bit storage schemes at <2% overhead.

Practical constraints / notes:
- Need a curated, privacy-safe sample trace. Ask data-ops for an anonymized day (JIRA:INF-889).
- For synthetic straggles, ensure the harness supports per-expert artificial delays; talk to Devin about extending bench harness.
- Memory: bounded re-quantization must be scheduled off-peak in Dedicated. Add operation window in rollout docs (CON-OPS-312).

Questions for the team / open puzzles:
- How to choose an "importance" score that generalizes across domains? (attention magnitude alone seems brittle).
- Is there a cheap proxy for hallucination severity that scales (beyond simple NLI/ROUGE heuristics)?
- Do we have safe anchors (golden prompts) that are stable across model versions for regression checks?

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Draft minimal bench repo skeleton: trace replayer + eviction toggles + simple scoring hooks (owner: me).
- [ ] Request anonymized session trace from data-ops (owner: Devin). JIRA INF-889
- [ ] Sync 30m with Mira to align severity rubric and plan a 1-week labeling blitz for probe bank.
- [ ] Prototype deterministic routing toggle in local runner and run a small 1k-request smoke test.

Notes-to-self (stylistic): keep experiments tiny and reproducible; focus on marginal differences (delta in p99, delta in severity-weighted hallucination) instead of absolute numbers. Save plots with raw traces and aggregated distributions.

References / links to read later:
- adaptive-kv-2026.pdf (local)
- sysml-moe-routing-2027-slides.pdf
- quant-stability-blog (internal link)
- CON-OPS-312 (confluence)

End.

(If I don't get to this: at least capture the trace and the rubric — rest can be iterative.)
